title: Tenants: declare GPU workloads with priority, condition, busy probe and drain
description:
## Summary

A `tenants` config section lets llama-broker decide which GPU workload gets the card, not just which model answers the next request.

## Current behavior

llama-swap (v262) loads whatever a request names. Groups (swap, exclusive, persistent) and `routing.scheduler.settings.fifo.priority` only order the waiting queue (fifo.go:381-389); nothing ranks workloads, nothing reacts to an outside condition, and the only hook is `hooks.on_startup` (config.go:138-143). A swap waits for in-flight HTTP requests (fifo.go:131-135, 207-215) but cannot see async work such as a job that keeps running after its HTTP request returned.

## Desired behavior

- Config: `tenants:` map, each entry with `models` and/or `groups` it owns, `priority` (int), `condition` (HTTP probe URL with expected status/JSON path, or a command whose exit code decides; polled at an interval), `busy` probe (same forms), `drain` action (HTTP call or command) and `vram` need.
- A tenant whose condition is true "wants the GPU". llama-broker never loads a model of a lower-priority tenant while a higher one wants the GPU and would not fit; such a request waits or gets HTTP 503 with a reason, per tenant setting.
- To make room for a higher tenant, a lower one is drained (busy probe until false, bounded by `unloadTimeout`) and then stopped.
- When the higher tenant no longer wants the GPU, held requests proceed.
- Tenant code lives in its own package (e.g. internal/tenants) with small hook points in the scheduler (fifo.go) and process stop path (process_command.go:805), so rebases onto upstream stay small.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unit tests: a lower-tenant request while a higher tenant's condition is true is held/refused; a busy lower tenant is drained before stop; held requests run once the condition clears.
- [ ] An end-to-end test with two fake upstreams (one "busy" for N seconds) shows the order of drain, stop and load in the log.

title: Weekly cloud routine: merge the newest llama-swap release, build, test, report
description:
## Summary

A weekly Claude Code cloud routine keeps llama-broker current with upstream llama-swap and reports success or failure.

## Desired behavior

- Routine name `llama-broker upstream sync`, cron `0 13 * * 1` (Mondays 13:00 UTC, 9:00am EDT), model claude-sonnet-5-5, repo https://github.com/McBrideMusings/llama-broker, tools Bash/Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep, no connectors.
- Environment: `Default` first; one trial run; if the build cannot fetch from GitHub or the Go module proxy, switch to `Unconstrained`.
- Each run: add `upstream` (mostlygeek/llama-swap), fetch tags, find the newest release tag. If main already contains it, build and test anyway and report "up to date". Otherwise MERGE the tag into main (never rebase, never force-push main); resolve conflicts by keeping upstream code and re-applying our hook lines, never deleting our files. Build and test per the repo's Makefile/README/CLAUDE.md, at least the Go build and `go test ./...`. Green: push main. Red or unresolvable conflict: push the attempt to `sync/<tag>` only.
- Report: try `gh issue create` titled `upstream sync <tag>: success | up to date | failed` with tag, previous tag, merge commit, conflicts and resolutions, commands run and results, failing output tail, branch pushed; if issue creation fails, say so. The run's final message carries the same report, first line `RESULT: ...`, then `ISSUE: <url or reason>`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The routine exists and its trial run's log shows the build and test result and whether the issue was created.

Blocked: the agent-dispatch-guard hook in Claude Code settings denies every RemoteTrigger call, so the routine cannot be created from a session until that hook asks instead of denying (or the routine is created by hand at claude.ai/code/routines with the settings above). Provenance: wow-private chatter design interview, 2026-10-03, questions 26-28.

title: Tenant decision log and GET /api/tenants status
description:
## Summary

Every brokering decision is logged and the current state can be read by a program.

## Desired behavior

- One log line per decision: time, tenant, condition/busy probe results with raw values, action (hold, refuse, drain, stop, load), reason.
- `GET /api/tenants`: each tenant's priority, condition state and last probe time, busy state, loaded models, held request count, and the VRAM figures.
- Decisions also go out on the existing `GET /api/events` stream.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After the ComfyUI drain test, the log alone explains every step, and `GET /api/tenants` matches what is loaded.

title: ComfyUI as a tenant: queue as busy probe, /free as drain
description:
## Summary

A documented, tested tenant recipe for ComfyUI, the first non-LLM workload.

## Current behavior

docs/kb/guides/upstreams/comfyui.md runs ComfyUI through `cmd: docker run --rm ...`, `cmdStop: docker stop ...`, `checkEndpoint: /`, `unloadTimeout: 30`, reached at `/upstream/<model>/...` with websockets. ComfyUI's `POST /prompt` returns at once and the job runs on, so a swap can kill a render mid-job. Discussion #962 tried a draining `cmdStop` loop; it failed with exit status 2.

## Desired behavior

- Busy probe: `GET /queue` — busy while `queue_running` or `queue_pending` is non-empty.
- Drain: hold new `/prompt` requests, wait for the queue to empty, `POST /free` with `{"unload_models":true,"free_memory":true}` (applied after the current prompt, ComfyUI server.py:1200-1209 at v0.38.0), then stop.
- A guide page with the full tenant entry.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With a real ComfyUI job running, a higher tenant's condition turning true lets the job finish, frees VRAM, then loads the higher tenant; a `/prompt` sent during the drain is held until ComfyUI may run again.

title: VRAM reserve kept free for workloads outside llama-broker
description:
## Summary

A configured amount of VRAM stays free for GPU users that llama-broker does not manage (video transcoders, for example).

## Desired behavior

- Top-level `vramReserve` (MiB). Tenant `vram` needs plus the reserve must fit the card's total, read from the hardware detection already in v262; a load that would break it is treated like a higher tenant holding the GPU.
- `GET /api/tenants` reports total, reserve, and each loaded tenant's need.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With a reserve set, a model whose declared need would cut into it is held, and the log says why.
